About the exercise

About the science behind Unrot

Unrot is inspired by J. P. Guilford’s Alternate Uses Test, a classic divergent-thinking prompt that asks people to imagine many new uses for an ordinary object.

Divergent thinking is about range, not perfection. The score breaks the round into four plain-language dimensions: fluency, flexibility, originality, and plausibility and elaboration.

  • Fluency tracks how many distinct ideas you found.
  • Flexibility tracks how many conceptual directions you changed into.
  • Originality tracks how rare each idea is for the same object.
  • Plausibility and elaboration track whether the idea is understandable and workable enough to picture.

Inspired by divergent-thinking research. This is a creative exercise, not a medical or diagnostic assessment.
